name: Array Traversal and Indexing
explanation: Arrays store elements in contiguous memory locations allowing O(1) random access via 0-based indices.
learning_objectives: Understand contiguous index calculation and offset arithmetic
Recognize time tradeoffs between indexed lookup O(1) and linear search O(N)
common_misconceptions: Confusing array length with the last valid index (length - 1)
Expecting element lookup by value to be O(1) without an index or auxiliary map

no_hint.message: Your array indexing logic is coming along nicely. Keep tracking your loop counters.
no_hint.next_step: Double-check your loop bounds to ensure you cover every valid element.
no_hint.reflection_question: What is the index of the final element when the array has length N?

concept.message: Arrays provide O(1) direct access by index, but searching for an arbitrary value requires O(N) linear scan.
concept.next_step: Consider whether checking values requires scanning the remaining array elements.
concept.reflection_question: If you need to look up values repeatedly, how does linear array iteration affect your total time complexity?

guided.message: Iterate through the array while keeping track of current element indices.
guided.next_step: Write a single loop starting at index 0 and ending at array length minus 1.
guided.reflection_question: What variable are you using to track the current position in the array?

pseudocode.message:
FOR i FROM 0 TO length - 1:
    element = arr[i]
    PROCESS element
pseudocode.next_step: Implement the array iteration loop in your programming language.
pseudocode.reflection_question: How do you guarantee that your index i never exceeds length - 1?

full_solution.message: Iterating over an array element by element allows inspecting or updating each item in linear time O(N).
full_solution.next_step: Test your solution with empty arrays and single-element inputs.
full_solution.reflection_question: Why is random element insertion inefficient in a standard contiguous array?

reflection_questions: How does 0-based indexing affect your loop condition (< N vs <= N)?
What occurs when you access index arr[len]?
pseudocode:
FOR i = 0 UNTIL array.length:
    current = array[i]
    IF condition(current):
        RETURN i

complexity.time: O(N) - Linear iteration across array elements
